title: FuncGraph: Geometry-Compiled Variable-Phase Conditioning for Frozen VLA Policies
hook: On terminal-pose-matched unseen object pairs, the same relation can require a different first contact and phase order, so full-task success is predicted to improve even when terminal-pose error does not. The claim is not that another PointMap adapter helps pi0.5, but that compiling two PointMaps into an ordered, point-bound functional program changes the action sequence.
hook_shape_rationale: Shape (a), surprising empirical reveal: the named outcome is full-task success on a terminal-pose-matched pair-composition split, where the predicted direction can diverge from final-pose error because the required first contact and phase order change. Shape (c) was also viable because pi0.5 remains frozen or lightly adapted, but it was rejected as the hook because parameter efficiency does not establish the functional-geometry mechanism.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier leaf demonstrates that the same named manipulation relation remains correct on unseen target-reference pairs when pair geometry changes both the initial grasp/contact choice and later alignment, approach, placement, or phase order; the anchor setting is MATCH POLICY's rigid key-frame transfer, while SPOT, MIMO, CoA-VLA, and EasyInsert expose adjacent pose-trajectory, relation-field, affordance-chain, and fixed multi-phase instances without closing this class-level requirement — stakes: a robot can choose an unrecoverable grasp or collision-prone approach even when its final pose estimate is accurate, while reported pose or scene generalization can be mistaken for functional compositional generalization and fail to transfer.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by replacing static PointMap injection with a variable-length, point-bound functional program that selects contact anchors, local relation frames, gripper modes, and phase order, then structurally conditions successive pi0.5 action chunks; corpus support is thin for robotics, with the closest C24 exemplars redesigning conditioning interfaces outside manipulation.

gap_closure.gap: The correspondence and relative-pose leaves inherit the assumption that transporting a demonstrated object-relative geometric target preserves the functional validity of the demonstrated grasp and motion template; none tests whether that invariance is necessary across functionally different but spatially registrable pairings — stakes: registration can be numerically excellent yet transfer the wrong contact semantics, and published gains attributed to 3D geometric generalization may rest on an unexamined equivalence between spatial match and functional interchangeability.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by a terminal-pose-matched pair-composition split that holds relation, individual-object exposure, and scripted goal transform fixed while independently varying the oracle contact-and-phase program; corpus support is thin in robot manipulation, so the C02 recipe is instantiated with MuJoCo contact state and pre-registered human real-robot labels as an oracle independent of the evaluated policy.

core_mechanism: FuncGraph keeps the OpenPI pi0.5 vision-language and action-generation backbone fixed and redesigns only the interface through which target-reference geometry controls successive action chunks. For target and reference PointMaps P_T={(x_i,f_i)} and P_R={(y_j,g_j)}, x_i and y_j are observed 3D coordinates in the calibrated robot frame and f_i and g_j are their provided PointMap features; a lightweight relation-conditioned compiler emits a functional program Z=(z_1,...,z_m), with m no larger than M_max=6 by default and M_max reselected as the smallest cap covering all phase runs in the training demonstrations. Each token z_h=(a_h^T,a_h^R,F_h,c_h,e_h) contains normalized attention distributions over the two observed point sets, anchors p_h^T=sum_i a_hi^T x_i and p_h^R=sum_j a_hj^R y_j, a predicted 6D relative frame F_h, a gripper/contact mode c_h, and an END decision e_h, so every program element is computable from the inputs and compiler readouts rather than from an external planner. The variable-length token order is the pair-specific interaction graph O: its nodes bind actions to surface locations and relation frames, and its directed chain is the structural prior that prevents the same terminal goal from implying the same grasp or approach. RoboCasa/MuJoCo contact logs and successful demonstration trajectories provide independent training targets for token anchors, modes, order, and END, while the modest FG-Compose-Robot resource supplies manually clicked surface anchors and phase boundaries for real demonstrations; a same-relation, terminal-pose-matched program-swap classifier is trained after program reconstruction so object identity and final pose cannot suffice. The active token is embedded as a structured key-value prefix to pi0.5, with the backbone frozen and only the compiler, a phase-transition head, and conditioning-projection LoRA of rank r_L=8 trained; r_L is selected from {4,8,16} by held-out full-task success under a matched trainable-parameter budget against a dense PointMap-prefix baseline. After each generated action chunk, the transition head reads the new observation, robot state, and active token and advances when its calibrated probability exceeds tau_adv=0.5, with tau_adv reselected on validation to maximize phase-boundary F1, so changing a token changes the next pi0.5 forward pass and therefore the physical action rather than only an auxiliary score. The C02 diagnostic uses RoboCasa asset recombinations in which each target and reference object appears in training but the ordered pair is held out, and a stricter subset shares the same scripted terminal transform while MuJoCo collision/contact state specifies different valid programs. A full-observation oracle gate replaces learned Z with the MuJoCo-derived program in simulation and a pre-registered human program on the available real robot; this separates failure of geometry-to-program compilation from failure of the frozen/light pi0.5 executor to use the program.
core_mechanism_reasoning:
PREMISES ledger:
P1. For the scoped rigid-object relations in RoboCasa and the real-robot set, the visible target-reference surfaces plus the relation contain enough information to identify action-relevant contacts and ordering; this is plausible because contact affordances are geometric, but it is untested — falsification target.
P2. Successful demonstration contact transitions and gripper-state changes provide usable weak phase supervision; MuJoCo exposes exact contacts, while real demonstrations receive modest manual boundary and surface-click annotation.
P3. A frozen or rank-limited pi0.5 executor has sufficient action competence once the active contact/frame token is explicit; the full-observation oracle gate tests this rather than assuming it.
OBSERVATION-MODEL premise. The provided PointMaps are visibility-censored surface samples from calibrated depth views, not unbiased samples of complete object geometry; training therefore uses the same view process plus point dropout, and the claim is scoped to relations whose decisive contact regions are observed.
ESTIMAND. The primary estimand is expected full-task success over ordered target-reference pairs drawn from held-out compositions, conditional on both individual objects and the relation appearing in training, with a secondary estimand restricted to terminal-pose-matched pairs whose oracle programs differ.
NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT — branch (i). The runnable naive version concatenates dense target and reference PointMap tokens plus the relation into pi0.5 through a generic prefix/adapter and trains the same LoRA parameters; it silently assumes end-to-end attention will preserve target/reference role binding and infer phase topology when object identities are recombined, a premise made false by the matched composition construction because identical terminal targets coexist with different required contact programs. FuncGraph confronts that failure head-on through point-bound ordered tokens, program-swap identification, and active-token advancement, rather than adding a larger encoder to the naive adapter. STANDARD-TOOL FOLLOW-UP. Structured prediction and hybrid-state estimation are standard tools, but the domain-specific unresolved structure is their coupling to partial 3D role binding, variable program length, and a frozen action-chunk generator under unseen pair composition; if the program is removed, the remaining dense adapter is explicitly treated as the baseline, not as a contribution.
DESIGN RATIONALE. The diagnostic sibling shares machinery with the method because the same program Z that conditions execution is the independent oracle variable used to construct terminal-pose-matched controls; without that split, the method claim is not identifiable. Alternatives rejected were a terminal SE(3) trajectory, which cannot represent changed contact semantics or phase count; a fixed textual affordance list, which repeats CoA-VLA's abstract-level scaffold; a hand-written task-and-motion schema, which regresses to PDDLStream-style planning; and a generic PointMap adapter, which leaves the composition shortcut intact.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Build FG-Compose-Sim by recombining existing RoboCasa target and receptacle assets under a fixed named relation, assigning every object to training with other partners while holding out ordered pairs; output ordinary pairs plus a terminal-pose-matched subset with MuJoCo contact/collision oracle programs.
2. Convert each successful RoboCasa demonstration into supervision by reading PointMaps, end-effector poses, gripper commands, and MuJoCo contacts; output an ordered sequence of point anchors, relative frames, gripper modes, and END, and create the same fields for the modest FG-Compose-Robot demonstrations by pre-registered human clicks and phase boundaries.
3. Implement the relation-conditioned compiler over P_T and P_R so it autoregressively emits z_h and END up to M_max; input is the two observed PointMaps plus relation text, and output is program Z with explicit point distributions and frames.
4. Train the compiler first on program reconstruction, then train a binary program-swap objective using same-relation terminal-pose-matched foils; output a compiler whose own program matches its pair and rejects a functionally different swapped program without using the action policy.
5. Add a structured-token prefix and phase-transition head to the existing OpenPI pi0.5 code path, freeze the base vision-language and action generators, and expose only rank-r_L conditioning LoRA plus the two small heads; output an active-token-conditioned action-chunk policy.
6. Train the LoRA and transition head on the same pi0.5-compatible demonstrations used by the dense PointMap-prefix baseline, matching data, trainable-parameter count, and compute; output matched checkpoints in which only the functional interface differs.
7. At inference, compile Z once from the observed pair and relation, inject z_h before every pi0.5 action forward pass, execute the resulting chunk, update the observation, and advance or retain h using the transition head; output a closed-loop trajectory whose grasp, approach, alignment, and phase count can change with the pair.
8. Evaluate dense PointMap prefix, fixed terminal-pose/trajectory conditioning, FuncGraph, token-permuted FuncGraph, and oracle-program FuncGraph on FG-Compose-Sim; output full-task success, first-contact correctness, phase-order edit distance, collision rate, and final-pose error on ordinary and terminal-pose-matched composition splits.
9. Freeze all hyperparameters and run the same learned, permuted, and pre-registered-oracle conditions on FG-Compose-Robot using the available real-robot platform; output an ecological-validity check rather than generalizing the claim beyond the evaluated rigid-object relations.
falsification_prediction: The minimal experiment fine-tunes only the FuncGraph compiler, transition head, and rank-limited conditioning LoRA around OpenPI pi0.5 on FG-Compose-Sim, then evaluates ordinary and terminal-pose-matched held-out target-reference compositions in RoboCasa and the modest FG-Compose-Robot real-robot set. If the mechanism works, full-task success and first-contact correctness increase while collision rate and phase-order edit distance decrease relative to the parameter-matched dense PointMap-prefix and terminal-pose baselines; final-pose error alone need not improve. The single load-bearing variable is the ordered point-bound functional program Z: permuting Z among terminal-pose-matched pairs while leaving observations, relation, weights, and action sampler unchanged should return downstream full-task success toward the dense-prefix baseline. As an oracle gate, replacing learned Z with the MuJoCo contact-derived program in simulation or the pre-registered human program on the real robot must improve the same downstream metric; if oracle Z does not help, the proposed interface/executor mechanism is falsified, whereas an oracle-only gain falsifies the geometry-to-program compiler premise.
compute_budget: 36 A100-80GB-equivalent GPU-days on the available 4xA100 node for compiler training, matched LoRA baselines, and repeats; $0 API. The modest FG-Compose-Robot resource adds 3 real-robot days and 300 evaluation trials, including oracle, learned, and permuted-program arms.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: Abstract-only inference: MATCH POLICY registers pick/place targets to stored key frames, whereas FuncGraph constructs from an unseen object pair a variable-length, surface-bound contact-and-phase program whose first grasp and ordering may differ despite the same terminal transform.

Abstract-only inference: SPOT conditions execution on an object-centric SE(3) pose trajectory already supplied by demonstrations, whereas FuncGraph predicts from pair geometry which contact frames exist and how many ordered phases the frozen/light VLA should execute.

Abstract-only inference: CoA-VLA injects a fixed four-part affordance chain, whereas FuncGraph grounds a variable-length program in explicit target/reference surface distributions and tests it on terminal-pose-matched unseen compositions with an independent oracle.

Abstract-only inference: MIMO constructs an implicit multi-feature field for shape reconstruction, similarity, and spatial relations, whereas FuncGraph constructs an ordered executable program that binds those pair-specific geometric distinctions to successive pi0.5 action chunks.

what_step_was_missed: Abstract-only inference: CoA-VLA would have needed to replace its predefined object-grasp-spatial-movement sequence with a pair-geometry-compiled, variable-length set of surface-bound contact/frame tokens, plus demonstrate that those tokens change execution on terminal-pose-matched unseen object compositions under an independent oracle.
